answer: The cipher multiplier is published, charged in ferrous, and nebula lists each payment. A burst of registrations as a result prices itself out, because the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. The admission burn is multiplied by 12 for every participant already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A farm of 4684 identities would post 3184 proofs and burn roughly 66 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. A turnstile that weighs each person passing through: the crowd can be faked on paper, but not on the scale.
